item.title: Senator Moody Votes to Pass College Sports Act with 20-Team Conference Cap
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody voted Monday to pass the Protect College Sports Act after successfully amending the legislation to expand the conference cap from 19 to 20 teams — a change she said was critical for Florida universities. Moody took to the Senate floor to offer the amendment, which passed by voice vote and became part of the final bill. "I've…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody voted Monday to pass the Protect College Sports Act after successfully amending the legislation to expand the conference cap from 19 to 20 teams — a change she said was critical for Florida universities.

Moody took to the Senate floor to offer the amendment, which passed by voice vote and became part of the final bill. "I've worked hard to improve this bill and support our Florida universities, and I'm proud of the result," Moody said in a statement. "Increasing the conference cap from 19 to 20 was vital to future of Florida schools' ability to continue to thrive in college athletics."

The move drew support from major Florida institutions including the University of Miami, Florida State University, and the University of South Florida, all of which have been advocating for changes to strengthen college sports regulation. Moody said she would continue to fight for Florida universities on athletic matters.

item.title: 19th Annual Bud Light Charity Tennis Tournament returns Oct. 16-17
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola Sports and The Lewis Bear Company are inviting tennis players to compete in the 19th annual Bud Light Charity Challenge Tennis Tournament, taking place October 16–17 at Roger Scott Tennis Center. The two-day event pairs competitive play with food, drinks, a silent auction, and courtside entertainment, with all registration fees…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Sports and The Lewis Bear Company are inviting tennis players to compete in the 19th annual Bud Light Charity Challenge Tennis Tournament, taking place October 16–17 at Roger Scott Tennis Center. The two-day event pairs competitive play with food, drinks, a silent auction, and courtside entertainment, with all registration fees supporting Arc Gateway and Pensacola Sports.

Over the past decade, the tournament has raised more than $115,000 for Arc Gateway, which provides programs and services for more than 1,200 children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. "The Bud Light Charity Challenge is more than a tournament — it's a celebration of our community," said Jason Libbert, President and CEO of Pensacola Sports. "It brings people together from every corner of our city for a weekend that's full of energy and purpose."

Advanced registration is $80 per player, with tournament-week registration at $90. Spectators can attend free, though food and beverage passes are available at Friday check-in for $15 (one day) or $25 (both days). Family, friends, and tennis fans are welcome to watch the matches. More details and registration are available at PensacolaSports.org/bud-light-charity-challenge. Pensacola Sports is also seeking volunteers for the event.

The Jay location typically operates Wednesdays only.

Residents and businesses needing tax collector services should plan accordingly or visit the offices on another day. More information about services and holiday closures is available at srctc.com.

item.title: FEMA Awards $116 Million to Florida for Hurricane Recovery and Resilience
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: FEMA is distributing more than $116 million to Florida for 88 recovery and resilience projects in the wake of recent hurricanes, including Milton, Debby, and Ian. The funding is split between immediate recovery assistance and long-term mitigation efforts designed to protect communities from future storms. The bulk of the money—more than $66…
item.content:encoded:
FEMA is distributing more than $116 million to Florida for 88 recovery and resilience projects in the wake of recent hurricanes, including Milton, Debby, and Ian. The funding is split between immediate recovery assistance and long-term mitigation efforts designed to protect communities from future storms.

The bulk of the money—more than $66 million—will go through FEMA's Public Assistance program to reimburse communities for debris removal, emergency response, and repair of critical infrastructure. Manatee County is receiving the largest single award at nearly $44 million, primarily for clearing more than 1.2 million cubic yards of debris from roads and public property. Lee County will get more than $3.8 million for debris removal and beach park repairs, while Pinellas County receives over $1.8 million for damage assessments and emergency measures.

The remaining $50 million will fund hazard mitigation projects through FEMA's Hazard Mitigation Grant Program, supporting proactive measures such as elevating flood-prone structures, improving drainage systems, adopting stricter building codes, and upgrading utilities and infrastructure to withstand future storms. No specific local Panhandle projects were detailed in FEMA's announcement, though these funds typically flow to counties statewide as applications are approved.

item.title: Escambia County OKs $894.5M budget after debate over sheriff funding
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The board split on whether to make deeper cuts to the sheriff's office and other constitutional officers' budgets. According to Coral Springs News,…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County commissioners voted Tuesday to approve a nearly $894.5 million budget for the coming fiscal year, but the decision didn't come without significant disagreement over spending priorities.

The board split on whether to make deeper cuts to the sheriff's office and other constitutional officers' budgets. According to Coral Springs News, commissioners debated the proposals at length before ultimately moving forward with the spending plan.

The approved budget will guide county spending across all departments and agencies over the next fiscal year. The final vote reflected disagreement among commissioners about the right balance between maintaining law enforcement and other core services.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Proposes Healthcare Reform Plan Featuring 'Trump Health Freedom Accounts'
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled the next phase of his "Rescuing America" initiative on Monday, introducing a healthcare proposal he says would lower costs and expand consumer choice in the insurance market. Scott's "More Affordable Care Act" centers on establishing what he calls "Trump Health Freedom Accounts"—HSA-style accounts that would…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled the next phase of his "Rescuing America" initiative on Monday, introducing a healthcare proposal he says would lower costs and expand consumer choice in the insurance market.

Scott's "More Affordable Care Act" centers on establishing what he calls "Trump Health Freedom Accounts"—HSA-style accounts that would deliver federal healthcare subsidies directly to individuals rather than to insurance companies. The proposal maintains key elements of the Affordable Care Act, including protections for pre-existing conditions and the existing healthcare.gov exchange system, while adding new competitive mechanisms.

The plan would allow Americans to purchase health insurance across state lines through a state waiver program, increase price transparency requirements for medical services, and enhance tax credits for small businesses offering coverage. According to Scott's office, the funds in the Health Freedom Accounts could be applied to premiums but would be restricted from covering abortion services or plans, in compliance with Hyde Amendment restrictions.

"Costs went up, people lost their doctors, and American families are still struggling for affordable healthcare solutions," Scott said in a statement, criticizing what he characterizes as the failures of the Affordable Care Act. "With simple fixes, we can bring more transparency to drive down costs and let families choose the plan that best fits their needs."

item.content:encoded:
The Southern Youth Sports Association is holding a grand opening today for the Rafferty Center, a new 10,000-square-foot community facility at 1301 West Gregory Street in Pensacola. The ribbon cutting is scheduled for 11:45 a.m., with media setup beginning at 11:30 a.m.

The center includes a multi-sport gymnasium, spectator seating, classrooms, study areas, and a concession stand. According to the media advisory, the facility will expand youth sports programming, tutoring, and after-school activities for SYSA members and the surrounding community. SYSA founder Lumon May and donors will participate in the ceremony.

Parking is available along Gregory Street, in front of the Theophalis May Community Center and the new Rafferty Center. Media interested in coverage can contact Travis Peterson at (850) 501-5262 or Lorraine Jessup at (850) 777-0165.

item.title: Florida Agriculture Department Protects 4,500+ Acres Through Land Preservation Program
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson announced today that the state has permanently protected more than 4,500 acres of working agricultural land through the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, bringing the statewide total to over 251,000 acres since the program's inception. The preservation happens through rural lands…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson announced today that the state has permanently protected more than 4,500 acres of working agricultural land through the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, bringing the statewide total to over 251,000 acres since the program's inception.

The preservation happens through rural lands protection easements that prevent future development while allowing farms and ranches to continue operating and contributing to Florida's economy. Properties remain in private ownership and on tax rolls, avoiding new state costs. Commissioner Simpson said the program represents "smart conservation" that protects Florida's food supply and rural communities without the traditional burden of public land acquisition.

Two Lake County properties were among those approved in today's Cabinet action: Blandford Farm & Ranch, a 349-acre sod and hay operation that secured a $7.5 million easement, and Encore Farms, a 194-acre horse and cattle operation that received a $5.4 million easement. Nearly 186,000 of the program's 251,000 preserved acres have been protected during Simpson's tenure as agriculture commissioner.

item.title: Santa Rosa County to Reformat Land Development Code for easier upkeep
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is preparing to streamline its Land Development Code through an administrative reformatting that will make the document simpler to maintain and navigate—but won't change any actual development rules. The proposed ordinance would repeal and replace the existing code solely to address formatting and organizational problems.…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is preparing to streamline its Land Development Code through an administrative reformatting that will make the document simpler to maintain and navigate—but won't change any actual development rules.

The proposed ordinance would repeal and replace the existing code solely to address formatting and organizational problems. Currently, the code relies on page numbers in its Table of Contents to help users find information, but those references become inaccurate whenever the code is amended and text shifts between pages. The new format will eliminate page number references and use section numbers as the primary navigation tool, with section numbers also added to document footers for consistent reference points even as the document grows or shrinks.

The Santa Rosa County Zoning Board will review the proposed ordinance at 5 p.m. Thursday, October 8, with the Board of County Commissioners scheduled to consider it at 5 p.m. Thursday, October 22. For details, contact Shawn Ward, Planning and Zoning Director, at ShawnW@santarosa.fl.gov or 850-981-7082.

item.title: West Garden Business Association launches to boost Pensacola's downtown beyond Palafox
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The group aims to shine a spotlight on the West Garden area and its merchants, positioning the neighborhood as an alternative shopping and dining…
item.content:encoded:
A newly formed West Garden Business Association is working to raise the profile of Pensacola businesses outside the traditional Palafox Street corridor, according to reporting from All for Gardening.

The group aims to shine a spotlight on the West Garden area and its merchants, positioning the neighborhood as an alternative shopping and dining destination within downtown Pensacola. By pooling resources and coordinating promotion, the association hopes to draw more foot traffic and customer attention to businesses that have historically operated in the shadow of Palafox's more established retail presence.

The effort reflects a broader strategy among local business leaders to diversify downtown's commercial appeal and support merchants in emerging neighborhoods. The West Garden area has seen growing interest from entrepreneurs and small business owners looking to establish themselves in walkable, accessible parts of the city.

item.title: 19th-century shipwreck debris surfaces on local beach after nor'easter
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A nor'easter that swept through the area recently exposed what may be the remains of a 19th-century shipwreck along a local beach, according to WPMI NBC 15. The discovery came as heavy seas and storm surge from the coastal storm churned up sand and debris along the shoreline. Pieces of what researchers believe could be ship wreckage — likely from…
item.content:encoded:
A nor'easter that swept through the area recently exposed what may be the remains of a 19th-century shipwreck along a local beach, according to WPMI NBC 15.

The discovery came as heavy seas and storm surge from the coastal storm churned up sand and debris along the shoreline. Pieces of what researchers believe could be ship wreckage — likely from the 1800s — washed ashore during the weather event.

While details on the exact location and condition of the wreck remain limited, such discoveries along Northwest Florida's coast are not uncommon. The region has a long maritime history, and nor'easters regularly unearth artifacts and debris from vessels lost centuries ago. Experts may examine the remains to determine the ship's identity and origin.

item.content:encoded:
Danielle Arion Bell, who disappeared as a 14-year-old Tate High School student in September 2001, remains missing a quarter-century after she vanished from a party in Cantonment.

Bell was last seen at a gathering in the 500 block of Cedar Tree Lane, in the area between Highway 29 and Highway 95A in North Escambia County. The case has gone unsolved for 25 years, making it one of the longest-running missing persons investigations in the county.

Authorities continue to seek information from the public about Bell's disappearance. Anyone with details about her case or her whereabouts is urged to contact the Escambia County Sheriff's Office or local law enforcement.

item.title: AAA: 66% of Floridians See Kids Riding E-Bikes Without Helmets as Injuries Spike
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new survey from AAA – The Auto Club Group reveals a widespread safety concern across Florida: nearly two-thirds of adults have witnessed children riding e-bikes or e-scooters without helmets, even as medical injuries from these devices surge among young riders. The findings come as pediatric emergency departments nationwide report a sharp uptick…
item.content:encoded:
A new survey from AAA – The Auto Club Group reveals a widespread safety concern across Florida: nearly two-thirds of adults have witnessed children riding e-bikes or e-scooters without helmets, even as medical injuries from these devices surge among young riders.

The findings come as pediatric emergency departments nationwide report a sharp uptick in e-bike and e-scooter injuries. According to a medical study cited by AAA, injuries among children and adolescents jumped 7.5-fold between 2023 and 2026, with more than a third of those cases involving head or neck trauma and nearly 7% resulting in traumatic brain injuries. The American College of Surgeons notes that only about one-third of injured riders were wearing helmets at the time of their crash.

"Many parents see e-bikes and e-scooters as just another version of a bicycle, but some of these devices can reach much higher speeds," said Mark Jenkins, AAA spokesman for The Auto Club Group. "With higher speeds come greater risks." The survey also found that 83% of Floridians support helmet requirements for e-bike and e-scooter riders, and 59% believe insufficient riders wear them.

In Florida, riders under 16 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting national safety standards, but local governments can adopt stricter rules. AAA emphasizes that helmet protection should match device speed: CPSC-certified bicycle helmets work for traditional bikes and slower devices (up to 20 mph), while NTA 8776 helmets suit higher-speed e-bikes (up to 28 mph), and DOT-certified motorcycle helmets offer the most protection for devices exceeding 28 mph.

item.content:encoded:

The arrest comes as law enforcement agencies across the region continue to respond to threats made against local establishments. Anyone with information about the incident is urged to contact Fairhope Police Department.

item.content:encoded:
A new survey indicates that Pensacola residents favor returning the city's Grand Mardi Gras Parade to Palafox Street, where it ran for 24 years before being relocated, according to WKRG News 5.

Tony Vance, president of the Krewe of Cheers, noted the parade's long history on the downtown street. "We've always rolled down Palafox Street," Vance said.

The survey results could influence city decisions about future parade routes as organizers weigh community input on where Pensacola's signature Mardi Gras celebration should take place. Details about the survey's scope and methodology were not immediately available.
